Brief statement of reasons for decision :
1.

Briefly stating, the case of prosecution, as mentioned in the charge-sheet, is that on 23.02.2016,
on receipt of DD No.28A from RTRM Hospital, J.P. Kalan regarding admission of Smt. Laxmi by her husband namely Sonu, who had some unknown poison, ASI Om Prakash alongwith Ct. Jitender reached RTRM Hospital and obtained MLC No.950/2016 of Smt. Laxmi on which the doctor had opined the patient to be 'unfit for statement' and referred the patient for Higher Centre, Safdarjung Hospital.

On coming to know that marriage of Smt. Laxmi was solemnized on 19.04.2015, ASI Om Prakash telephonically informed Sh. Suchet Singh, Tehsildar, Executive Magistrate, Najafgarh about the incident and also informed parent of Smt. Laxmi.
Thereafter patient Smt. Laxmi was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital where Sh. Ramphal and Smt. Krishna - parent of Smt. Laxmi met him.

On the directions of Executive Magistrate, ASI Om Prakash produce the parents of Smt. Laxmi before the Executive Magistrate, where parents of Smt. Laxmi stated that they would give their statement later.
Thereafter, on 25.02.2016 vide DD No.9A information was received from Safdarjung Hospital regarding death of Smt. Laxmi.
The said information was conveyed to Executive Magistrate and dead body was got preserved.
Thereafter, ASI Om Prakash reached the State vs. Sonu & Ors.
PS:Jafarpur Kalan office of Executive Magistrate where statement of Sh. Ramphal, father of deceased Laxmi was recorded by Executive Magistrate.
2. In his statement, the complainant Sh. Ramphal - father of deceased Laxmi stated that his daughter Laxmi, aged 20 years, got married to accused Sonu on 19.04.2015 according to Hindu rites.
After three-four months of marriage of Laxmi, her in-laws started demanding for a car but he told them that he had three daughters and he was unable to give any car to them.

Sh.Ramphal further stated in his statement that whenever Laxmi came to her parental home, she informed them that as and when her sister-in-law (Nanad) came to their house, her Nanad alongwith Sonu, Smt.
Raj and Sandeep - husband, mother-in-law and brother-in-law of deceased respectively, used to beat her and make a demand of car from her and that if she did not fulfill their demand, they would kill her.
He also stated that on 23.02.2016 at about 12:00 midnight, accused Sonu informed them on telephone that Laxmi ate poison and he was taking her to RTRM Hospital.
Thereafter, they reached RTRM Hospital where the doctor referred Laxmi to Safdarjung Hospital where she died on 25.02.2015 at about 05:00 AM.

Sh. Ramphal - father of deceased further stated that his daughter Laxmi did not have poison and he suspected that Sonu (husband), Raj (mother-in-law), Sulekha (sister-in-law) and Sandeep (brother-in-law) forcibly administered poison to Laxmi.
He prayed for legal action against them.
3. On the basis of above statement of the complainant, ASI Om Prakash prepared Rukka and got the FIR registered against the accused persons.
After registration of FIR, further investigation was marked to Insp. Sudhir Kumar.
During further State vs. Sonu & Ors.
PS:Jafarpur Kalan investigation
, inquest proceedings were conducted and dead body was sent for postmortem.
Thereafter, accused persons namely Sonu, Raj and Rekha @ Sulekha were arrested.
Since State vs . : Sonu & Ors.

Further, exhibits were sent to FSL for examination.

After completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed before the Court of Ld. M.M.
4.
After compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C., the case was committed to the Court of Sessions and was assigned to Ld. Predecessor of this Court.

5. After hearing arguments on the point of charge, Ld. Predecessor of this Court was pleased to frame the charge for offence punishable u/s 498-A/304-B/34 IPC and in the alternative, under Section 302/34 IPC against all the three accused persons, vide order dated 31.08.2016, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
6. During trial, the prosecution examined 17 witnesses in all, in support of its case.
7. Statements U/s 313 Cr.P.C. of the accused persons were recorded during which all the incriminating evidence which came on record, were put to them, which they denied.
The accused persons claimed that they are innocent and no demand of dowry was made by them.
They also stated that no poison has been consumed by Laxmi and that she got unconscious on 23.02.2016 and they got admitted at RTRM Hospital.
They further stated that Laxmi mostly used to remain at her parental house and about 20 days before the incident, she came back from her parental home.
She mostly used to remain unhappy while State vs. Sonu & Ors.

PS: Jafarpur Kalan coming back from her parental house and when they used to ask her about her unhappiness, she told them that she was not willing for this marriage as she wanted to get married with someone else but her parents forcibly married her to accused Sonu.
Accused persons opted to lead evidence towards their defence.

8. However, despite giving sufficient opportunities, accused persons had not examined any witnesses in their defence and upon their submissions that they do not want to lead any DE, DE was closed Court on 21.01.2020.
9.
Before discussing the rival submissions made on behalf of both the sides, it would be appropriate to discuss, in brief, the testimonies of prosecution witnesses which have come on record.

The said testimonies are detailed as under:-
10.
PW1 Sh. Ramphal/complainant (father of deceased Laxmi) stated that his daughter Laxmi was married to accused Sonu on 19.04.2015 according to Hindu rites and customs.

After 3-4 months of marriage, the accused persons i.e. Sonu (husband), Raj (mother-in-law), Sulekha (Sister-in-law/Nanad) and Sandeep (brother-in-law/Devar) started demanding a four wheeler car from Laxmi.
As and when Laxmi came to her parental house, she used to disclose about the said demand of dowry by the accused persons.
When PW1 visited the matrimonial home of Laxmi, he made understand the accused persons that he was having three more daughters and was not in a position to fulfill their demand of car.
About a week before the death of Laxmi, she visited their home and at that time she told that 'papa, mera pati, meri saas aur meri nanad mere saath maar pitai karte hain aur car ki manng karte hain'.
After 2-5 days of coming of Laxmi to their house, all accused persons including Devar of Laxmi came to State vs. Sonu & Ors.
PS: Jafarpur Kalan their State vs . : Sonu & Ors.

When they insisted for taking Laxmi to her matrimonial house,
Laxmi told him that 'ye mere ko zeher dene ki dhamki de rahe hain aur ye mere ko jaan se maar denge'.
However, after tendering the apology, all the accused persons proceeded for their home on his request that he would send his daughter after 4-5 days.

PW-1 further stated that after 4-5 days,
he sent his daughter to her matrimonial home with accused Sonu who came to take Laxmi on his request.

After one week, during the month of February and March, 2016, he received a call on his mobile from his son-in-law Sonu, who told that Laxmi had consumed poison and that they were taking her to RTRM hospital.

Thereafter, he alongwith his wife, son and nephew, who is driver by profession, reached RTRM Hospital in a Maruti Van, where they came to know that Laxmi was referred to Safdarjung Hospital, so they went to Safdarjung Hospital and found his daughter Laxmi in almost an unconscious condition.
On that day, he alongwith his wife remained in the hospital.
On the next day at about 05:00 AM, the attending doctor informed that Laxmi had died.

Thereafter,
IO/ASI Om Prakash, who was present in the hospital, recorded his statement.
He alongwith his wife, son and other relative were also taken to office of SDM, Najafgarh, where his statement Ex.PW1/A was also recorded by SDM.
His wife also endorsed his statement.

Thereafter, they went to Mortuary of Safdarjung hospital and after postmortem, he received the dead body of his daughter Laxmi vide receipt Ex.PW1/B.

During postmortem, the viscera of the body was preserved for which saturated solution of common salt was used as preservative.

On the basis of FSL report pertaining to viscera of deceased, postmortem report and inquest, he opined that the possibility of Organophosphorus poisoning and its complication as cause of death cannot be ruled out and he has proved his said opinion as Ex.PW2/B.

She requested the accused persons that their financial position is not sound and they could not fulfill their demand of car.

He also deposed that in his presence,
Laxmi did not tell about the demand of dowry and of vehicle by her in-laws or about beatings being given to her by her brother-in-law and mother-in-law.

Since PW5 turned hostile from his earlier statement made before the police, he was cross examined at length by learned Addl. PP for the State but nothing fruitful came out during his cross examination.

During his cross examination, he has specifically denied the suggestion that his statement Mark-PW5/A was recorded or that after 3-4 months of the marriage of his niece, her in-laws started making demand of dowry.

He has also denied the suggestion that when his niece used to visit his house, she used to complain to him that her husband, brother-in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law used to beat her and used to make demand for a vehicle.
He has also denied the suggestion that he suspected on the accused person that they administered some poison to Laxmi as a result of which she died.

498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.

Explanation.

304B. Dowry death.

Parents of the deceased are presumed to be in knowledge of all the facts whichever they can on 24.02.2016 which they had stated on next date i.e. on 25.02.2016.
Therefore, there is an unreasonable delay of about 1 day in lodging of the FIR.
51. It is held by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Ramesh & others Vs. State of The NCT of Delhi 2012 IX AD (Delhi) 15
On account of delay, the report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, but danger creeps in of introduction of coloured vision, exaggerated account or concocted story as a result of deliberation and consultation".
52. Other witnesses examined by the prosecution are formal procedural witnesses who had completed the investigation and statement of any of the such official witnesses is not sufficient to link any of the accused persons with the commission of the offence alleged against him.
53. In view of aforesaid discussion, Court comes at the conclusion that prosecution has failed to establish its case against any of the accused persons for the offences under Sections 498- A/304-B/34 IPC as well as for the alternate offence punishable under Section 302/34 IPC beyond reasonable doubt.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Benefit of doubt goes to accused persons.
Hence, all accused persons namely Sonu S/o Late Sh. Raj Kumar, Smt. Raj W/o Late Sh. Raj Kumar and Smt. Rekha @ Sulekha W/o Sh. Madan Kumar stands acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 498- State vs. Sonu & Ors.
Previous bail bonds of the accused persons stands cancelled and sureties stands discharged.
Fresh bail bonds and surety bonds u/s 437-A Cr.P.C. are furnished on behalf of all accused persons and same are accepted till six months from the date of judgment.
